summary: Quarterly operations sync focused on recent outage retrospective, capacity and hiring prioritization, product roadmap adjustments, and risk mitigation. Leadership reviewed metrics, decisions on immediate hiring vs delay tradeoffs, and agreed to follow-up doc and postmortem.
topics: Capacity planning and Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs
Hiring priorities for infra and SRE
transcript:
Header: 2026-03-21 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~75m | Location: All-hands Townhall - Zoom
Attendees: Jordan, Mira, Leo, Dana, Tom, Priya + company-wide
---
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we' re gonna kick off, um, short and focused ops lighthouse and decision standup. Big thanks to folks who stayed late on the rollback on Thursday.
[00:20] Mira Gupta: Quick housekeeping, the A/V is fine i think, if you're on phone, please mute, we'll have Q&A at the end.
[00:35] Jordan Patel: Mira, can you lead with the incident summary — top line, what happened, how we responded, where we landed?
[00:45] Mira Gupta: Yeah, top line: last wednesday, 3/18, we saw a regional capacity squeeze that cascaded into increased latency and then a small but visible error surface for some hosted customers. The root trigger was an autoscaler regression combined with a kernel selection mismatch when a model variant hit a higher sequence length distribution. In plain english, two things lined up: an autoscaling change pushed more requests onto a small pool and the runtime selected non-optimal kernels, so tail latency spiked.
[01:30] Leo Kim: to add, the KV cache eviction policy also behaved unexpectedly under burst, so cache misses amplified the CPU and GPU work per request.
[01:45] Mira Gupta: We rolled traffic to Dedicated pools, throttled some non-prod workloads, and pushed a quick rollback to the autoscaler flags. That stabilized within about 18 minutes for most traffic, full remediation took about 2 hours due to backfill of queued work.
[02:10] Jordan Patel: Priya, quick customer impact note from finance / commercial? Any churn risk flagged?
[02:20] Priya Nair: We flagged a handful of mid-market accounts — outreach is ongoing, no escalations to execs. Estimated revenue at risk negligible short-term but we're tracking sentiment. We should plan to offer a postmortem note to impacted accounts by EOD Friday.
[02:45] Dana Alvarez: Product perspective — we need to add a canary traffic policy into the rollout flow for kernel/runtime changes and model variants. The current rollout assumes identical perf characteristics which is not true.
[03:05] Jordan Patel: Agree. Okay, high level decisions we need today: 1) approve postmortem timeline and owner, 2) decide on immediate hiring top-ups for SRE vs delay, 3) any quick gating for runtime changes.
---
[05:00] Mira Gupta: On the postmortem: i'll own the draft and share with the execs, want input from eng leads and SREs. I'll include timeline, root cause, detection & response, and remediation and follow-up.
[05:18] Leo Kim: I'll coordinate the runbook changes and follow-ups; we should add a section on autoscaler rollout guardrails.
[05:30] Jordan Patel: Sounds good. Tom — hiring. We had proposed 6 infra hires this quarter. Do we accelerate or push?
[05:40] Tom Rivers: Hiring pipeline is thin, our current time-to-hire is about 8 weeks for Sr infra. We can accelerate by opening two urgent SRE roles to contractors or temp hires, but that increases cost. If we delay hires, we risk capacity and longer-term technical debt. Need triage decision: hire 2 immediate, defer 4?
[06:05] Priya Nair: From runway and budget, hiring 2 senior SRE contractors is feasible if we accept a 10% OPEX increment this quarter. Hiring 6 full-time staff would materially change burn.
[06:25] Jordan Patel: Let's tentatively approve 2 immediate SRE contractors and reconvene mid-next-week with a final plan.
---
[07:00] Dana Alvarez: Roadmap changes: we will push the next-quarter experimental kv-cache-optimizer to mid-Q3 to reduce risk; instead we'll prioritize rollout guardrails for kernel selection and canarying. This is a product-engineering tradeoff but reduces immediate exposure.
[07:30] Leo Kim: We'll create a canary policy that ties sequence-length histograms to kernel selection tests before global rollout. That should catch these cases in staging/canary.
[07:50] Mira Gupta: Also adding an autoscaler simulation harness into CI so we can test burst patterns with realistic request traces.
---
[09:00] Jordan Patel: Questions from the floor? I see a hand from Emma in Amsterdam, go ahead.
[09:10] Speaker 3 (Emma - Eng): Quick— are we changing SLA commitments for hosted customers while we patch? Will that be visible?
[09:20] Priya Nair: No SLA change planned. We're adding transparency and will notify impacted accounts with a short note and timeline. Ops will proactively reach out to higher-touch customers.
[09:40] Speaker 4 (Sam - Product): Are dedicated customers affected?
[09:45] Mira Gupta: Minimal for dedicated, because Dedicated pools were used as fallback. But we need clearer routing policies and docs for customers to pin model variants or request capacity guarantees.
---
[12:00] Jordan Patel: Ok team, let's talk risk & compliance quick wins — two items. One: increase visibility of audit logs for private deployments. Two: re-evaluate KMS key rotation cadence for the next quarter.
[12:20] Leo Kim: On audit logs, we'll roll a shallow retention extension for private deployments by the end of next sprint and surface the logs in the console. Might need customs from security.
[12:40] Tom Rivers: From people side, we need to ensure oncall bandwidth matches the new retention and runbook changes; will propose a 2-week rotation bump for SRE if contractors join.
---
[15:00] Jordan Patel: Quick metrics readout — Priya? Top-line ARR, bookings, churn signal?
[15:10] Priya Nair: ARR growth on track to 28% YoY; bookings slightly light vs plan this month. Churn is stable — the incident added a small uptick in NPS for a subset but we're addressing with outreach and credits. Cash runway unchanged at ~18 months.
[15:40] Jordan Patel: Good. Any major hiring or comp notes?
[15:45] Tom Rivers: Compensation calibration is scheduled next week; we may need to hold off on new bands for ICs until runway sensitivity review is complete.
---
[18:00] Dana Alvarez: Quick product demo note — we'll have a short internal demo next Thursday of the canary tooling. Expect invites.
[18:15] Jordan Patel: Great. Final section: decisions recap and owners. Mira writes postmortem draft; Leo scopes runbook & canary; Dana reprioritizes roadmap; Tom opens two contractor reqs; Priya sends updated runway note.
[18:40] Mira Gupta: I'll include a timeline and a proposed customer communications template; please review in 24 hours.
[19:00] Jordan Patel: Question queue — we'll try to get to as many Qs as possible in 20 minutes. Remember the Qs: folks want more transparency into change windows and canary policy.
---
[20:00] Audience Q: "Will we change the default route for non-prod bursts?"
[20:10] Leo Kim: Yes, we'll start to throttle non-prod by default during high load windows and enable a burst window template for teams that need it.
[20:30] Audience Q: "When will runbooks be updated?"
[20:40] Mira Gupta: Initial runbook patch in 72 hours, full iteration in two sprints.
---
[30:00] Jordan Patel: ok last few items — governance ask: align execs on capex vs opex tradeoffs for Dedicated expansion. We'll set up a 30m follow-up next Tues.
[30:20] Priya Nair: I'll bring models: expansion capex vs reserved capacity costs and margin sensitivity.
[30:35] Jordan Patel: Wrap — thanks, team. Action items and owners as noted. We expect the external postmortem and comms draft by Friday and will follow up in the next all-hands.
[30:50] Jordan Patel: Meeting adjourned.
